title: Next-Year Share for Reserves That Pay Tax Installments Separately
content:
Where a Summit Tax and Insurance Reserve under Set-Aside Accounts pays each property tax installment separately (as the plan schedule of charges paid shows), the next-year share in its tax projection follows the installments themselves.

**Tax year's bills**: the property tax bills on file for the reserve received no later than the review date and fewer than 12 whole calendar months before it. A tax year has 2 installments.

- **Installment count basis.** Where the plan pays tax installments separately and at least two of the tax year's bills are paid or received, the next-year share is the number of the tax year's paid bills divided by the number of installments in a tax year, 2 — because each installment the reserve has already paid is followed within the coming twelve months by the next tax year's matching installment.
- **Annual block basis.** Where the plan pays tax installments separately and exactly one of the tax year's bills is paid or received, the next-year share is one when the due date of the most recently received property tax bill is on or before the review date, and zero otherwise. The most recently received bill is the property tax bill on file with the latest received date, whatever its status.
- In any other case this rule does not set the share.

| Tax year's paid or received bills | Of which paid | Most recently received bill due | Next-year share |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 2 | — | 1 |
| 2 | 1 | — | one half |
| 3 | 1 | — | one half |
| 1 | — | On or before the review date | 1 |
| 1 | — | After the review date | 0 |
